Generate random FASTQ record indices for sampling

Source: R/vtamR_fun.R
sample_fastq_indices.Rd

Generates a random subset of FASTQ record indices for sampling from one or two FASTQ files. When two FASTQ files are provided, their record counts are checked to ensure that they contain the same number of reads.

Usage

sample_fastq_indices(
  fastq1,
  fastq2 = NULL,
  n,
  randseed = NULL,
  quiet = TRUE,
  chunk_lines = 1e+05,
  fast_count = TRUE,
  total_reads = NULL
)

Arguments

fastq1

Character string giving the path to the first FASTQ file.

fastq2

Optional character string giving the path to the second FASTQ file. This is typically the mate FASTQ file for paired-end sequencing. If supplied, it must contain the same number of records as fastq1. Omitting fastq2 is faster because the record count of a second FASTQ file does not need to be checked. In this case, the correspondence between the number of reads in fastq1 and a potential second FASTQ file is not verified.

n

Integer specifying the number of records to sample. Sampling is performed without replacement.

randseed

Optional integer used to initialize the random number generator with set.seed. Setting this argument makes the generated indices reproducible.

quiet

Logical indicating whether progress messages should be suppressed.

chunk_lines

Integer specifying the maximum number of lines read at a time when counting FASTQ records. Defaults to 1e5.

fast_count

Logical value controlling the counting method. When TRUE on Linux, shell commands are used for faster counting. When FALSE, the chunk-based R implementation is used on all operating systems. This argument is passed to count_reads.

total_reads

Integer or NULL. The total number of sequences in the input file, if already known (e.g. from a pre-computed value or an info file). If NULL (the default), the function will count the sequences in the file itself, which can be slow for large files. Supplying total_reads skips this counting step and uses the given value directly, so it is the caller's responsibility to ensure it is correct.

Value

A list with two elements:

total

The total number of FASTQ records in fastq1.

keep_idx

A sorted integer vector containing the indices of the records to retain. If n is greater than or equal to the total number of records, NULL is returned, indicating that all records should be retained.

Details

The function does not read or extract the selected records. It only counts the input records and generates the indices of the records to retain. These indices can subsequently be used to extract the same subset from paired FASTQ files.

FASTQ files are expected to contain four lines per sequencing record. Record counts are obtained using count_reads.

When fastq2 is provided, its record count is compared with that of fastq1. The function stops with an error if the two files contain different numbers of records.

If n is smaller than the total number of records, n unique record indices are sampled using sample.int and returned in sorted order. If n is greater than or equal to the total number of records, no sampling is necessary and keep_idx is set to NULL.

See also

count_reads, sample.int

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Generate indices for sampling 10,000 reads
idx <- sample_fastq_indices(
  fastq1 = "reads.fastq",
  n = 10000,
  randseed = 123,
  quiet = TRUE
)

# Generate shared indices for paired-end FASTQ files
idx <- sample_fastq_indices(
  fastq1 = "reads_R1.fastq.gz",
  fastq2 = "reads_R2.fastq.gz",
  n = 10000,
  randseed = 123,
  quiet = TRUE
)
} # }
